NONE: › in poetry, the continuing of a sentence from one line of a poem into the start of the next line
› formal to tell someone to do something or to behave in a particular way
› US specialized law to legally force someone to do something or stop doing something

example: [ + to infinitive ] We were all enjoined to be on our best behaviour.
我們都被叮囑舉止一定要得體。
He enjoined (= suggested) caution.
他囑咐要謹慎行事。

T: A1 to get pleasure from something

NONE: A2 to get pleasure from the situation that you are in
過得愉快；感到快樂；玩得痛快
› something you say to someone when you have given that person something and you want them to enjoy it

T: C2 to have something good or lucky

example: I really enjoyed that movie/book/concert/party/meal.
我真的很喜歡那部電影／那本書／那場音樂會／那次派對／那頓飯。
[ + -ing verb ] I want to travel because I enjoy meeting people and seeing new places.
我想去旅遊，因爲我喜愛結識不同的人，見識沒去過的地方。
I don't think Marie is enjoying herself very much at school.
我覺得瑪麗在學校不是太開心。
Come on, why aren't you dancing? Enjoy yourselves!
快過來，你們怎麽不跳舞啊？痛痛快快地跳吧！

More examplesI'm ready to go home now but I don't want to drag you away if you're enjoying yourself.The beer festival was a huge open-air event with music, stalls and everyone enjoying themselves.Time passes so quickly when you're enjoying yourself.Don't be spoilsport - let the children enjoy themselves a little!We all enjoyed ourselves tremendously at the party.
enjoy! informal
Here are your drinks. Enjoy!
這是您的飲料。請慢用！
Even though he's 86, he enjoys excellent health.
雖然都86歲高齡了，他身體依然很健康。

NONE: B1 An enjoyable event or experience gives you pleasure.
使人快樂的；令人愉快的；有樂趣的

example: a very enjoyable game/movie
其樂無窮的遊戲／引人入勝的電影
Thank you for a most enjoyable evening.
謝謝你，我們今晚很開心。

NONE: B2 the feeling of enjoying something

example: Knowing the ending already didn't spoil my enjoyment of the movie.
雖然我已經知道了電影的結局，但還是看得津津有味。
